title: LF advice on my workflow
author: TheKevinBoone
selftext:
Hi all, just wanted some advice on my current setup since I am dipping my toes in game dev now that it has become a lot more accessible and LLMs are getting increasingly effective at it. My current workflow looks as following:

Codex  
├── repo inspector  
├── Unity specialist  
├── test specialist  
├── edge-case reviewer  
└── ONE integration writer

Claude Code  
├── Unity reviewer  
├── animation reviewer  
├── architecture reviewer  
├── performance reviewer  
└── parent synthesizes findings

Antigravity  
├── web research  
├── licence research  
├── browser QA  
├── visual comparison  
└── parent synthesizes findings

I have a blender MCP and Unity MCP hooked up to Claude and have subscriptions for Claude, Chat GPT and Gemini. I am considering to get Claude Max (not sure if I want to go for 5x or 20x) since I’m hitting those 5g usage limits a lot but not sure if that’s worth it just for the Fable model considering my current stack. Antigravity I got fairly cheap for like a full year prepaid. ChatGPT is the Plus subscription and Claude is currently Pro.

What do you guys think, is it worth going for the Claude Max bump? Any advice or changes you think are worth it? Eager to learn from the more experienced devs and vibecoders out there

comments.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
comments.body:
I think in general your workflow is doing too much.  You really only need 1 AI (Claude does great) and just let it do it's thing.  You still need to provide the architecture, mechanics, ideas, and domain/computer science concepts knowledge so you can make sure it doesn't do anything crazy.

My current 4-repo project is 28k lines of Go, about 80k c# split across the remaining 3, and all of it is GOOD code that is easy to understand and efficient at what it does.  I've only used Claude, and a typical session barely uses any tokens (less than 1% of weekly on max 20x), takes less than 15 minutes, and stays lean, ending at <200k context.  It's all in how you set up the architecture and documentation/systems mapping to let 1 agent work quickly and efficiently.

This is, of course, just my opinion and experience though.

replies.author: TheKevinBoone
replies.body: Thanks, appreciate you taking the time to reply and providing these insights. My whole idea was that I would use the models depending on their specialism. GPT helps me with the architecture, Claude does most of the heavy lifting in terms of actual coding, Antigravity is the independent reviewer and wil suggest things in terms of UX/UI. You’d rather go with 1 agent and get Max 20x?

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body:
Yes, but let me reword my original comment a bit. I do also use chatgpt $20 plan, but only for describing architecture/etc and generating markdown documents for Claude to read, and only when it's actually a large enough task/change that I'd be worried about mistakes. I don't have them linked together at all, I just talk to chatgpt on High and describe what my original line of thinking was, have some back and forth to refine it, then tell it to make the idea into a markdown document. Then tell Claude "read docs/abc.md and create a plan, do not implement anything without asking."

It's worked well, because then you essentially get 2 rounds of AI revision/feedback on your original ideas before it gets worked.
